newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends with short covering gains.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends with short covering gains.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended higher across the board Tuesday in a moderate session, lifted by short covering after an early move down stalled at support despite reports of softer physical prices.
March climbed 5.7 cents to close at $2.224 per million British thermal units. April settled four cents higher at $2.147. Other deferreds ended up by 0.7 to four cents.

"Short covering - that's all it was. We couldn't quite get to the $2.12 low (in March), so they bought it back, but did you see the latest weather forecast?" said one Midwest trader, referring to a mostly-mild 10-15 day weather forecast.
Despite some colder Midwest weather this week, traders said a two week forecast released Tuesday called for mostly normal to above-normal U.S. temperatures.
"There's a little cold coming in the next few days, but it's only for one or two days," a Texas trader said.

And with eastern storage in good shape and likely to grow further in Wednesday's weekly AGA stock report, most expected cash and futures to stay on the defensive near-term though a technical bounce was not ruled out.
Withdrawal estimates for the AGA report ranged widely from 85 to 190 bcf compared to a 193 bcf adjusted draw the same week last year.
Chart traders still pegged key March support at the Nov 5 low of $2.12, with psychological buying likely at $2. Resistance was seen in the mid-$2.20s and then in the low-$2.50s.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices slipped more than five cents Tuesday to the low-to-mid $2.30s. Midcon pipes held relatively steady in the low-$2.30s. New York city gate gas was down about a nickel to the mid-to-high $2.80s.
The 12-month Henry Hub strip gained 2.7 cents to $2.161. NYMEX said an estimated 32,389 Hub contracts traded, up from Monday's revised tally of 30,773.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas did not trade Tuesday.

On the KCBT, March finished six cents higher at $1.99, while deferreds ended mixed. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.3 cent to 23.4 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 863 lots changed hands, up sharply from Monday's total of 263.
